summary.headline: Greaves Cotton Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 31% YoY to INR975 crores, but margins fell 2-2.5 percentage points on investments and commodity costs.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 31% YoY to INR975 crores and core businesses grew 16% to INR710 crores (19% like-for-like after portfolio exits). Margins came under pressure by 2 to 2.5 percentage points, which management attributed to about 1.5 points of deliberate Greaves.Next investments and commodity inflation (platinum, aluminium, steel, fuel) that pricing has only partly offset. Management said Q2 will be marginally better than Q1 and H2 better than H1, and that it remains committed to full-year FY27 margin targets. GEML revenue was about INR270 crores, roughly double last year, with market share reported at 5.6% in June.

segments.name: Energy Solutions
segments.commentary: Grew 21% YoY; medium-horsepower gensets grew 32% YoY. A pilot BESS facility was commissioned and a large institutional order covering supply, installation, commissioning and aftersales was executed.

segments.name: Mobility Solutions
segments.commentary: Grew 18% YoY; automotive engines grew 36% YoY. Retail aftermarket pruning is complete (2-wheeler spares, lead-acid batteries, multi-brand EV retail, farm equipment exited). Excel grew 14% YoY.

segments.name: Industrial Solutions
segments.commentary: Reported revenue flat YoY and 9% growth after portfolio rationalisation. FM-UL compliant firefighting engine exports started and a large defence order was completed.

segments.name: Greaves Electric Mobility (GEML)
segments.commentary: Record Q1 volume growth of 101% YoY vs industry 75%. Market share rose to 5.6% in June from 4.5% exit FY26; 2-wheeler revenue up ~120% and 3-wheeler up ~80% YoY. Dealer network expanded from ~300 to 600.

segments.name: Greaves Finance (GFL)
segments.commentary: AUM at INR560 crores, growing; Board approved an additional ~INR50 crores investment.

guidance_outlook: Greaves.Next target of 16-20% revenue CAGR for the next few years reiterated; management says it is on track for the 16% growth guided for the current period.
Price increases and cost-avoidance measures expected to show from Q2, with full benefit in H2 FY27.
Q2 margin expected marginally better than Q1; H2 expected to make up any H1 shortfall; full-year FY27 margin target reiterated.
GEML expected to move into positive EBITDA in 4 to 6 quarters; management declined to give specifics.
GEML double-digit national market share targeted in 4 to 8 quarters, based on roughly 1-1.5 points of share gain every 3 to 4 quarters.
Current capital infusion expected to fund GEML for about 2 years including capex, with burn rates now in single digits.
capex_capacity: GEML invested INR331 crores via rights issue (total INR530 crore issue, fully subscribed by GCL and Abdul Latif Jameel in proportion to holding).
GEML 2-wheeler production capacity is about 480,000 units.
Robotic gantry cell commissioned at CSN facility; Excel debottlenecking added 10-15% output; Excel pushpull cable utilisation at 70-75%, rubber line just starting.
Pilot Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) facility commissioned; commercial launch targeted in subsequent quarters.
Core business capex stated as on track; 650 kVA own engine launched last quarter.
demand_pricing: GEML 2-wheeler run rate roughly 9,000-10,000 units in the latest quarter; growing ~2,000 units per quarter.
Raw material price indexing for OEM contracts applies with a lag; aftermarket pricing passed through via distributors.

Strong demand for medium-horsepower gensets in industrial and commercial applications; AI data-centre demand described as strong, with a strategic supply agreement with a large global engine maker for larger sizes.
Excel: business restarted from Europe and expected from the US after a Russia-Ukraine-related export setback last year.
International business is about 13% of core revenue; Greaves International Trading FZE set up in Dubai for Middle East and Africa.

qa_highlights.question: How has margin erosion split between OEM and aftermarket/retail?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said commodity costs hit all products. OEM contracts have indexing with a lag, while aftermarket pricing is easier to pass on; price increases have been taken in both.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin drop is investment versus commodity cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Manish Poddar attributed about 1.5 percentage points to additional investments; the rest is the inflation-price lag, which should narrow in Q2 and fully in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is GEML's growth sustainable and when does it turn EBITDA-positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikas Singh said per-unit losses have fallen sharply and EBITDA could turn positive in 4 to 6 quarters, without committing to timing or scale.

qa_highlights.question: Why does GFL, an EV financing NBFC, exist in a pruned portfolio, and is it brand-agnostic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said GFL is part of the EV ecosystem; its share of GEML financing is near double digits and rising. Vikas Singh said financing partners are brand-agnostic by nature.

qa_highlights.question: Is there enough cash for the investee investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Manish Poddar said standalone liquidity as of March 2026 covers the INR50 crore GFL and INR331 crore GEML investments plus Q1-Q2 capex and dividends, and that the core business generates enough cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is motorcycle entry planned for GEML?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikas Singh said motorcycle prototypes are underway; the scooter opportunity is also large and prioritisation is under leadership review with no timing decided.

risks_watch: Margins: Q1 margin down 2-2.5 pts; recovery depends on Q2-H2 pricing and cost savings, and the full-year target is contingent on H2 catch-up.
Commodity and geopolitical cost pressure (West Asia developments) may outlast the pricing actions.
GEML is still loss-making with a 4-6 quarter timeline to positive EBITDA; management gave no firm timing.
Excel revenue of about INR66-70 crores and export-led recovery depend on new Europe and US customers.
Greaves Technologies had earlier slippages; management said it is still stabilising and cited one pilot design-work order.
Unallocable expenses of INR25.82 crores in segment results; the company said these are now folded into core business P&L (slide 27).
